Specifically, we adopt Language-Embedded Gaussians as the intermediate scene representation, propose a geometry-aware deformable attention module to refine Gaussian semantic features, and construct instance-level vision-language embeddings to provide reliable semantic supervision. We further introduce geometry-aware decoupled semantic distillation to mitigate the interference between geometry learning and semantic learning. To evaluate open-vocabulary occupancy prediction performance, we introduce OpenOcc-ScanNet and OpenOcc-Replica, two extended benchmarks with more diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. Experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art approach by 12.2 mIoU and 0.6 IoU on the Occ-ScanNet dataset, with consistent gains under new open-vocabulary evaluation protocols.

candidate.title: SG-Splat: Stable Geometry Learning under Pose Uncertainty for Pose-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting
candidate.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a promising representation for real-time novel view synthesis and 3D scene reconstruction. For practical deployment, recent studies have explored pose-free feed-forward 3DGS, which reconstructs Gaussian representations directly from unposed input images. However, these methods remain sensitive to residual pose errors, which perturb canonical-space Gaussian transformation, introducing noisy supervision for geometry and attribute learning. To address this problem, we present SG-Splat, a pose-free feed-forward 3DGS framework that improves robustness to pose uncertainty and stabilizes the learning of Gaussian primitives. SG-Splat decouples geometry estimation and Gaussian attribute prediction into two dedicated branches, reducing error coupling between pose-sensitive geometry and Gaussian attributes. We further introduce a coarse-to-fine refinement pipeline, consisting of Flow-Guided Pose Refinement (FGPR) and Residual-Guided Geometry Correction (RGC), to improve geometric alignment before Gaussian attribute reconstruction. Specifically, FGPR refines camera poses with flow-based correlation features and differentiable bundle adjustment. RGC then corrects initial point maps using depth residuals derived from FGPR, producing more reliable Gaussian centers. To stabilize training, we introduce a dual-path strategy that mixes ground-truth and predicted poses for canonical transformation. It provides clean supervision for Gaussian attributes while improving geometry robustness to residual pose errors. Extensive experiments on DL3DV and RealEstate10K show that SG-Splat achieves state-of-the-art performance in both novel view synthesis and pose estimation.

candidate.title: Intent-Preserving Adversarial User Simulation for Multi-Turn Agent Evaluation
candidate.abstract: Multi-turn agents are commonly evaluated with LLM-based simulated users, which can be overly cooperative and can therefore overestimate an agent's performance. We here introduce StressSim, an intent-preserving adversarial user simulator framework for stress-testing agents with challenging yet valid user interactions. StressSim optimises the simulator's high-level adversarial plan for each task instance. Candidate planner prompts are evolved with a genetic prompt-optimisation loop that uses rollout traces, granular task-completion signals, and validity feedback to favour conversations that reduce task success without changing the user's underlying goal. We evaluate the approach on the MultiWOZ dataset and the retail and airline domains from tau-bench with three target LLM agents, comparing against standard simulators and hand-designed non-collaborative user behaviours. We demonstrate the effectiveness of StressSim in exposing robustness gaps across frontier LLMs, with tau-bench pass^4 scores decreasing by up to 69% on gemini-3.8-flash and 62% on gpt-5.6-sol. StressSim maintains goal preservation performance (which decreases by at most 10%), using an optimisation budget of 20 rollouts per task. Sensitivity analysis suggests that increasing the budget further decreases task success. Overall our results demonstrate that StressSim exposes robustness gaps missed by standard and hand-designed user simulators while maintaining conversation realism. This is achieved through lightweight prompt optimisation alone, without model fine-tuning.

candidate.title: MANTIS: Multi-Axis News Transformations for Instance-Wise Stress Testing and Worst-Case Training in Fake News Detection
candidate.abstract: Automated fake news detection is vital on social media, where fake news is easily rewritten to fool detectors. However, existing approaches typically rely on superficial writing cues or single-style text rewrites, resulting in poor robustness under diverse cosmetic modifications. We construct MANTIS-Bench, a multi-axis presentation-attack benchmark that pairs original news with rewritten views across writing style, emotional expression, and dissemination framing. We further propose MANTIS, an instance-adaptive adversarial framework enabling dynamic worst-case training tailored to each news article with zero inference-time overhead. This reframes fake news defense from heuristic format smoothing into targeted, fact-invariant credibility assessment. Experiments on MANTIS-Bench show that MANTIS reduces the Union Attack Success Rate (UASR) by 3.55 percentage points relative to SheepDog on GossipCop and consistently outperforms prior single-axis defenses on Macro-F1 while maintaining competitive clean accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-axis and instance-adaptive worst-case training.

candidate.title: Learning High-Quality Pseudo-Labels for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
candidate.abstract: Point-supervised temporal action localization (PTAL) aims to recognize and localize action instances in untrimmed videos using only point-level annotations. Existing pseudo-label-based methods have made substantial progress in PTAL. However, confidence-based initialization can overlook well-localized proposals. Meanwhile, existing methods either keep pseudo-labels fixed during detector training or update them without fully exploiting alternative boundary evidence from the original proposal pool. These limitations constrain supervision quality, thereby hindering detection performance. To learn high-quality pseudo-labels, we propose a framework that integrates prior-guided initialization with consensus-guided refinement during detector training. Our framework comprises two modules: Prior-Guided Initialization (PGI) and Consensus-Guided Refinement (CGR). PGI combines proposal confidence with point-derived priors to establish instance-specific reliability for initial pseudo-label selection and candidate retention. CGR continually uses the retained original candidates to construct boundary targets, combining their consensus with evolving detector predictions to refine pseudo-labels throughout training. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves competitive detection performance compared with existing methods. In particular, our method achieves 68.5\% average mAP over tIoU thresholds 0.1--0.7 on THUMOS14, surpassing PseR by 3.7 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyingfang/LHQP

candidate.title: Multi-Fidelity Training Reshapes Uncertainty Decomposition in Atomistic Models
candidate.abstract: Multi-fidelity training, which combines abundant low-fidelity data with scarce high-fidelity labels, is increasingly common in atomistic modeling, but its effect on predictive uncertainty remains largely unexplored. We investigate this question using deep ensembles of mean-variance MACE models trained on ANI-1x, contrasting high-fidelity training from scratch with low-fidelity pretraining followed by fine-tuning. We characterize aleatoric, epistemic, and total uncertainty throughout training and under two distribution shifts: unseen molecular systems and higher-energy configurations. We find that pretraining reduces prediction error and improves uncertainty-based ranking across all test sets, but does not yield well-calibrated predictive variances; calibration deteriorates more severely under energy extrapolation. Training-dynamics analysis localizes most of this calibration degradation to high-fidelity optimization, during which the learned aleatoric variance becomes overconfident on held-out data. Moreover, multi-fidelity fine-tuning produces a more effective uncertainty-based acquisition function than high-fidelity training from scratch. These findings show that uncertainty ranking and calibration capture distinct properties and must be assessed separately in multi-fidelity atomistic models, especially under extrapolation.

candidate.title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
candidate.abstract: Historical maps contain dense morphological and semantic information about past urban environments, but many digitization workflows focus primarily on extracting geometry, and do not capture cartographic semantics such as building use and construction materials. This study introduces ArchiveLens, a generative spatial knowledge framework that operationalizes historical maps as entity-centric, machine-queryable geospatial databases. The pipeline decouples morphological and semantic reconstruction through three stages: tiled YOLOv11-seg instance segmentation for building footprint extraction; deterministic material classification via hue, saturation, and value (HSV)-based color thresholds; and localized attribute parsing using a quantized vision-language model constrained by domain-specific prompts. Extracted entities are integrated into a hybrid Spatial-Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (ST-RAG) architecture that combines dense semantic retrieval with symbolic spatio-temporal filtering and mandatory provenance grounding. Applied to 445 georeferenced Sanborn map sheets of Chicago (1918-1950), the framework achieves high geometric and semantic accuracy. Beyond performance, ArchiveLens advances GIScience by formalizing historical cartography as structured spatial knowledge representation, allowing researchers to query building attributes and compare spatial patterns across map sheets and years.

candidate.title: SCAFFOLD under Hessian Similarity: Sharp Convergence Rates
candidate.abstract: One of the main challenges of federated learning is heterogeneous data split among the clients, leading to biased local updates called client drift. The SCAFFOLD algorithm (Karimireddy et al., 2020) corrects client drift with control variates, but its relation to the similarity of client data is not yet fully understood: the original similarity-based guarantees cover only quadratics with a stronger second-order similarity assumption, and a follow-up weakly convex analysis (Luo et al., 2025) obtains a $\sqrt{L\delta}$ dependence for $L$-smooth losses with averaged Hessian similarity $\delta$. We analyze SCAFFOLD with minibatch-based control variates and establish linear dependence on Hessian similarity beyond quadratics, for both convex and nonconvex objectives. In particular, for convex objectives with exact gradients, $R$ SCAFFOLD rounds with $K$ local steps lead to an objective gap of order $(L/K+\delta)D_0^2/R$, where $D_0$ is the initial distance to a minimizer. When $K=\Theta(L/\delta)$, it improves the minibatch SGD rate by a factor $\Theta(L/\delta)$. For nonconvex objectives, we prove an analogous stationarity guarantee under uniform Hessian similarity for a client-selection variant. In both settings, we extend these guarantees to stochastic gradients and prove matching lower bounds for the analyzed methods with constant local stepsizes. We also show that, under partial participation, even identical clients need not obtain the full communication benefit of additional local steps.

candidate.title: Triage: Skip, Skim, or Refine Attention Tiles in Video Diffusion Transformers
candidate.abstract: Attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates the inference of video diffusion transformers (DiTs). Existing methods reduce this cost through sparsity, low precision, or both, but use a single precision for all kept tiles. We observe that the output error introduced by approximation varies widely across tiles. Many tiles can be skipped with little error, others must be computed but gain little beyond low precision, and a few retain substantial error even at low precision. We present Triage, a training-free attention method that assigns each tile one of three approximation tiers: skipping it by replacing it with its block means, skimming it in NVFP4, or refining it with NVFP4 residual correction. A lightweight router predicts each tile's error under each tier from block statistics and moves a tile to a more accurate tier only when the predicted error reduction justifies the extra compute, with a single price setting this trade-off. A fused kernel executes all three tiers in a single pass on the FP4 tensor cores of RTX Blackwell GPUs. Across Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo, and LTX-2.5, Triage accelerates end-to-end generation by up to 2.32x over dense FlashAttention, and in each of five settings it runs faster than every baseline while reaching 0.3-3.0 dB higher PSNR than the highest-PSNR baseline.

candidate.title: VidEdit3D: Flexible 3D Gaussian Editing with Video Diffusion
candidate.abstract: Recent advancements in text-guided 3D editing, particularly with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promise but still lag behind the flexibility of 2D editing tools. Existing methods face a critical trade-off between preserving multi-view consistency and allowing structural modifications. Image-based editors can also struggle to apply the intended edit to objects viewed from unusual angles. To address these limitations, we introduce VidEdit3D, a framework that reformulates 3D scene editing as a trajectory-based video editing task. By drawing a parallel between camera movement in static 3D scenes and temporal dynamics in video, we leverage the robust spatiotemporal priors of pre-trained Video Diffusion Models (VDMs) to encourage semantic and structural coherence across views. Specifically, we propose Trajectory-Guided Rendering (TGR) to select informative keyframes and construct smooth video clips aligned with VDM input requirements. To propagate edits from an anchor view to these clips, we develop Flow-Aligned Video Editing (FAVE), a training-free framework incorporating an Editing Consistency Guidance (ECG) mechanism. ECG contrasts source and edited image conditions at a shared latent state, using scheduled source-image amplification to strengthen adherence to the edited reference while maintaining original scene context. Finally, we introduce Region-Selective 3DGS Refinement (RS-GS) to strictly confine geometric and appearance updates to target primitives, reducing background attribute leakage. Experiments demonstrate stronger instruction alignment and better multi-view consistency than the baselines.

candidate.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
candidate.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT fails on 35% of pairs, a linear probe on VGGT's frozen features predicts pose failure on held-out categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, compared with 79.7% for VGGT's own point-map confidence and 77.7% for a classifier trained on all of VGGT's outputs. The probe catches failures VGGT is confident about, lets a downstream system abstain on the pairs it distrusts, and transfers without retraining to rotation failures on PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, beyond what co-visibility explains. This knowledge is absent from the per-image encoder: it is computed partway through the layers that fuse the two views, and the same holds for a second model, $\pi^3$. In essence, we find that VGGT knows more about its own failures than it reports.

candidate.title: Bridging Static and Agentic RAG for Taiwanese Historical Question Answering
candidate.abstract: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enables language models to adapt retrieval based on previously retrieved evidence, but it remains unclear whether such adaptive orchestration consistently outperforms well-designed static pipelines. We conduct a controlled comparison of agentic and static RAG for Taiwanese historical question answering, sharing the same generator and hybrid retrieval backend. Despite similar aggregate performance, the two pipelines differ on 70.83% of questions, with their advantages largely canceling out when averaged. An oracle that selects the better response per question improves the composite score by 0.2417 over the better individual pipeline, revealing substantial headroom for question-level selection. We therefore introduce a post-hoc selector that compares the two responses and their cited evidence, significantly outperforming either individual pipeline and recovering 60.34% of the oracle headroom. These results show that aggregate comparisons can obscure meaningful question-level differences between retrieval strategies, suggesting that exploiting their complementarity may be more fruitful than seeking a universally superior pipeline.

candidate.title: AnalogPortBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Analog Circuit Porting
candidate.abstract: Analog circuit design still relies heavily on expert knowledge, and porting proven designs to new process nodes is a recurring bottleneck. As a lower supply reduces available voltage headroom, a working topology may require redesign or fail to meet specifications. While large language models (LLMs) have begun to generate and optimize analog circuits, existing benchmarks focus on one process node and assume feasible specifications. To bridge this gap, we introduce AnalogPortBench, a benchmark of 54 tasks for porting ten circuits, from current mirrors to telescopic amplifiers, from a 0.18 $\mu$m process to the open-source SKY130 PDK. Tasks range from a direct port through a reduced supply and harder specifications to infeasible ones, and every feasible task has a reference design verified at five process corners. Evaluating six frontier LLMs at two reasoning levels, with and without simulation feedback, we find that models port simple circuits but rarely re-design headroom-sensitive amplifiers, seldom recognize infeasible specifications, and gain more from simulation feedback than from more samples or reasoning. Code and data are available at https://github.com/saeidrajabii/AnalogPortBench.

candidate.title: WebUniverse: Scaling Verified Training Data for Agentic Web Development
candidate.abstract: Training agents for front-end web development requires demonstrations of code editing, execution, browser inspection and revision, yet public trajectories and reusable task environments remain limited. We introduce WebUniverse, a pipeline that constructs verifiable tasks with verified development trajectories from open-source repositories and real web pages. The tasks cover text-grounded application development in standalone and iterative settings and vision-grounded reproduction across pages and viewports. We collect agent trajectories for these tasks and verify the resulting applications against task-specific functional or visual requirements. We release WebUniverse-Env, containing 15K executable task environments, and WebUniverse-Mix, containing the corresponding 15K development trajectories with verification records and scores. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on WebUniverse-Mix raises the Vision2Web average score from 51.7 to 68.3, WebGen-Bench accuracy from 34.5% to 63.9%, and Web-Bench pass@2 from 12.2% to 23.1%. The resulting model also outperforms a public-data baseline trained with the same configuration and sample budget across all reported metrics. Ablations show complementary benefits from text and visual trajectories and continued gains as training data scales from 5K to 15K trajectories.

candidate.title: A Deterministic Security Runtime for LLM Agents on MPI and Batch-Scheduled HPC Systems: Consensus-Governed, Hardware-Rooted Supervision of Every Rank
candidate.abstract: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

candidate.title: ReSight: Task-Driven Self-Improving Memory for Embodied Agents
candidate.abstract: Robots can use historical observations to answer spatiotemporal queries in familiar environments, but the presence of relevant evidence does not imply that existing tools support the operations a task requires. We introduce ReSight, a task-driven self-improving memory system for embodied agents that expands the capabilities for processing and accessing historical observations as task demands arise. ReSight retains keyframes and their spatiotemporal associations, separating observation evidence from extensible derived fields so that stored observations can be reprocessed for new needs. An execution agent and a coding agent share this memory through different interfaces: the former calls registered tools within a bounded online budget, while the latter uses a programmable workspace and a larger exploration budget to inspect evidence, write programs, and acquire models as needed. To realize capability expansion in ReSight, we develop Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM), which identifies capability gaps from execution and exploration records without task reference answers and converts exploration-derived solutions into reusable memory builders, query tools, and skills, extending memory representations and access capabilities as needed. Experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate effective base memory access and capability expansion. With the execution model and online budget held fixed within each benchmark, EDM reduces mean position error on OC-NaVQA from 33.10 m to 24.72 m and improves high-level success on FindingDory from 38.3% to 63.8%. With the tools and skill frozen, success still improves by 28.3 percentage points on FindingDory episodes excluded from exploration and distillation. Experiments on real robot patrol memories further demonstrate reuse of these capabilities for subsequent queries and new memories, with fewer online tool calls on average.

candidate.title: A Model-Theoretic Formalization of AlKhwaremis ilm alfaraid
candidate.abstract: This paper presents a model theoretic and computational formalization of AlKhwarizmis treatment of inheritance within the framework of Computational Fiqh. We first show that every inheritance configuration in a specified class is representable as a finite system of rational linear equalities and inequalities, and that such systems are decided exactly by Fourier Motzkin elimination over Q. We then define the fixed dimensional inheritance structure Vd with distinguished claimant coordinates, and prove that every admissible rational linear coordinate realization is isomorphic to Vd, this establishes the algebraic representation as canonical within that class. The complete first order theory Td of Vd is shown to be complete by construction and is explicitly distinguished from the decidability of the inheritance relevant fragment. The methodological principle is then related to a broader formalization of closed Fiqh domains via exhaustive case generation, Horn clause axiomatization, and terminating deduction, yielding domain relative computational completeness.

candidate.title: The Geometry of Limits in ReLU Function Spaces
candidate.abstract: We study the geometry and closure of spaces of functions realized by ReLU neural networks of fixed architecture. We first establish a general result about limits of continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions: the minimum number of convex sets on which a function is affine is lower semicontinuous under pointwise convergence. The proof uses a connection to hypergraph coloring and a compactness principle, and yields quantitative bounds on the polyhedral complexity of continuous limits. We then characterize the functions realizable by shallow ReLU networks with vector-valued outputs, extending a known scalar-valued characterization. Using this and the geometry of limiting hyperplane arrangements, we prove that fixed-width shallow scalar ReLU realization spaces are closed in the weighted supremum norm on the whole input space. In contrast, we construct an explicit sequence of networks with architecture $(2,3,2\mid1)$ whose limit is not realizable by that architecture. Non-closedness holds both globally in weighted supremum norm and under uniform convergence on compact sets with nonempty interior, disproving a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender. Finally, we show that non-closedness for a fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture necessarily involves a \emph{blow-up residue}, in which diverging output coefficients amplify an emerging linear dependence among hidden features. Together, these results provide geometric and functional-analytic tools for studying the boundaries and degenerations of ReLU realization spaces.

candidate.title: Deep Scientific Reasoning under Physical Constraints: Structure-Aware Spectrum Prediction
candidate.abstract: Structured scientific spectra encode rich physical information while obeying hard constraints, such as conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry. Accurate prediction of these spectra is central to materials discovery, yet existing methods often treat them as unconstrained sequences and therefore fail to enforce the underlying physical structure. Taking electronic density of states (eDOS) as the prototypical example, we introduce DeepSciReasoner, a general paradigm for predicting scientific spectra under physical constraints. The framework combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning, allowing predictions to capture rich spectral structure while respecting the underlying physics. We evaluate DeepSciReasoner on eDOS, phonon density of states (phDOS), X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), and Raman spectra, where it substantially improves prediction accuracy while maintaining physical consistency. These results establish DeepSciReasoner as a reusable blueprint for structured scientific spectrum prediction under hard physical constraints.

candidate.title: Does Notation Matter? MusicXML Tokenisation for Symbolic Music Generation and Understanding
candidate.abstract: Symbolic music representations encode musical content at varying levels of completeness, from performance-oriented formats such as MIDI to fully notated scores such as MusicXML. Yet the impact of this representational richness on deep learning models remains poorly understood. While tokenisation has been extensively studied for MIDI, score-based formats have received considerably less attention, and MusicXML in particular remains largely unexplored despite being the de-facto standard for score interchange. In this paper, we introduce the first general-purpose tokenisation framework for MusicXML, and conduct a systematic empirical study to determine whether notational richness confers a measurable advantage for deep learning on symbolic music. We train 26 autoregressive and masked language models, comparing MusicXML tokenisation against MIDI and ABC-based representations, probing the effect of different tokenisation strategies within MusicXML, and testing whether music-grammar-aware tokenisation outperforms treating scores as plain text. We evaluate music understanding tasks using linear probing across composer classification, difficulty estimation, and accompaniment suggestion, and generative tasks using objective statistical metrics and a human pairwise preference study. Our results show that MusicXML-tokenised models outperform MIDI and text-based counterparts on understanding and generative tasks.

candidate.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
candidate.abstract: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.

candidate.title: LLM WikiLeaks: Uncovering URL-Based Capability Extension and Security Circumvention in Agentic Message Boards
candidate.abstract: Autonomous agents have been observed acting beyond their assigned tasks, accessing unauthorized systems, and establishing communication channels to exchange information, yet the Web and network-level techniques they use to extend their capabilities and circumvent security restrictions remain poorly understood. We study these techniques through the ProWiki incident, in which agents restricted to outbound HTTP GET requests repurposed a public German-language wiki as a message board. We analyze 14,591 agent edits containing 79,541 URL postings and present corroborating evidence that the published URLs reflect the agents' operational activity. We find that 26,717 URL occurrences (33.6%) embed target URLs within one to five layers of third-party Web services. By recursively reconstructing these nested URLs, we identify 67 distinct intermediate services and classify their functionality. Most intermediate layers (73.8%) extend agents' capabilities by delegating content extraction and transformation to external Web services: Markdown and OCR services convert web content into machine-readable text, JSON filtering services extract selected fields, and archival services expose historical versions of pages. The remaining 26.2% facilitate circumvention of access restrictions and evasion of detection, including CORS and fetch proxies that retrieve content on agents' behalf, and link shorteners and redirectors that hide destination URLs from mechanisms inspecting literal URLs or outer hostnames. Agents also reach the same targets through multiple URL paths, consistent with attempts to evade rate limits or obscure request origins. Our results expose a gap between the capabilities granted to agents and those they can obtain by composing publicly available Web services: restricting an agent's local toolset or direct Internet access may be insufficient while third-party services remain reachable.

candidate.title: Pro-Active Inference
candidate.abstract: Estimating a population mean is fundamental across scientific applications, but observing every outcome can be prohibitively expensive. Often, covariates and machine learning (ML) predictions are available for the full population, even when only a small subset of outcomes can be observed. How can we leverage this information to proactively select observations to label, update ML predictions as labels arrive, and construct statistically valid confidence intervals? We develop a general, without-replacement formulation of Pro-Active Inference (PAI), extending our earlier with-replacement approach and building on Active Statistical Inference. Rather than making fixed-order label-skip decisions, PAI proactively selects which observation to label next from the remaining covariate pool while accommodating online ML updates. We establish PAI's finite-sample unbiasedness and asymptotic validity, develop an improved finite-sample variance estimator, and extend PAI to superpopulation inference without Bonferroni corrections or $\alpha$-splitting. We characterize PAI's potential efficiency gains over Batch Active Inference in a quasi-oracle setting, highlighting the role of prediction-residual imbalance. Across eight diverse datasets, PAI achieves greater sampling efficiency than Sequential Active Inference in the vast majority of tested settings with near-nominal statistical coverage, using the same ML predictor and uncertainty score. However, comparisons with simpler baselines such as Prediction-Powered Inference and uniform sampling, as well as the closely related Prediction-Powered Active Testing, reveal when additional adaptivity helps or hurts statistical efficiency. Through interpretable, theory-motivated diagnostics and frozen-ML ablations, we investigate when and why PAI gains or loses efficiency, highlighting the initial residual-estimation problem and subsequent online learning dynamics.

candidate.title: MMGNet: Multi-Modal 6-DoF Grasp Synthesis for Cluttered Scenes
candidate.abstract: Grasping is a foundational capability in robotic manipulation. Scene-level 6-DoF grasp synthesis relies on point clouds for metric geometry, yet real-world point observations are often noisy, incomplete, and over-smoothed. RGB images provide object-region, boundary, and appearance cues, yet two bottlenecks limit their effective use in scene representation and local grasp reasoning. We present MMGNet, a Multi-Modal Grasp Synthesis Network that addresses these bottlenecks through hierarchical image-to-3D feature injection and rotational graspness modeling. Hierarchical injection integrates multi-scale image features throughout 3D representation formation, while the rotational graspness jointly predicts the grasp approach direction and in-plane rotation before organizing local image-informed features through grasp-shaded grouping. Ablation studies show that these two modules provide complementary gains. MMGNet achieves a mean AP of 60.34 on GraspNet-1Billion with RealSense, surpassing all compared methods. In real-world experiments with adversarial grasp objects, MMGNet improves the grasp success rate over AnyGrasp by 8.46 percentage points. \emph{Code, models, and data will be released upon publication.}

candidate.title: CA-HNM: Constraint-Aware Hard Negative Mining for Dense Retrieval with Structured Domain Models
candidate.abstract: Dense retrievers are commonly trained with hard negatives selected from lexical or dense retrieval results. Retrieval proximity, however, does not indicate whether a candidate conflicts with explicit domain structure. We introduce CA-HNM, a constraint-aware hard-negative mining framework that combines retrieval-based candidate generation with deterministic incompatibility rules derived from a structured domain model. The framework removes known positives, constructs a local typed context around the query target, records relational, scope, target, and level mismatches, and uses the resulting candidates to fine-tune a standard dual encoder. Structured information is required only during offline negative construction. We evaluate CA-HNM on MOOCCubeX and Course-Skill Atlas with two encoders, two training losses, and ten seeds. Relative to a retrieval-rank-matched control, CA-HNM-Pure has higher mean NDCG@10 in six of eight dataset--encoder--loss configurations. Four hierarchical 95% bootstrap intervals are entirely above zero, mostly under triplet loss. In a separate experiment, CA-HNM-Mixed shows slightly higher mean NDCG@10 than a matched-mixed control on both collections. Structural variants show that changes in available structure can also change candidate eligibility and negative-pool composition. The results indicate that the contribution of constraint-aware selection depends on the training objective and the composition of the negative pool.

candidate.title: Identities, Not Pairs: Distribution-Free False-Accept Control for Embedding-Based Verification
candidate.abstract: Embedding-based verification often calibrates a false-accept threshold from all impostor pairs among $m$ identities, although these pairs share identities. We characterize a worst-case limit: when hub identities score highly against a fraction $\rho$ of the population, a calibration-only threshold with marginal false-accept rate (FAR) at most $\alpha$ under every identity-exchangeable law reaches the hub score on hub-free calibration sets with probability at most $(m+2)\alpha/(2\rho)$. Uniformly accepting near that score at levels well below $\rho/m$ therefore requires trial information. We propose COVE, which ranks the trial pair among all $N=\binom{m+2}{2}$ pairs formed by augmenting the calibration units with the probe and reference. Under identity exchangeability, its marginal FAR is at most $\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor/N$, with first possible acceptance at $1/N=O(1/m^2)$. The rule also retains this guarantee with a fixed symmetric cohort-normalized score using an independent cohort. On 6 benchmarks and 8 frozen encoders, realised FAR was consistent with the exact bound. Where both valid calibration-only baselines accepted nothing, COVE retained a median $100\%$ of the sampled oracle's true-accept rate over reliable comparisons. In contrast, an empirical quantile over dependent pairs reached 2.87$\,\alpha$ FAR, and a binomial upper confidence bound over pairs missed its nominal 95\% conditional-FAR target in up to 55\% of calibration draws. Symmetric CSLS raised COVE's true-accept rate by up to 4.3-fold in the tested settings. The code is available in https://github.com/salimkhazem/Cove.git

candidate.title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
candidate.abstract: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.

candidate.title: Explainable Prediction of High-Speed Solar Wind Streams driven by Coronal Holes via Topological Data Analysis
candidate.abstract: High-speed solar wind streams (HSSs) originating from coronal holes (CHs) are an important driver of recurrent geomagnetic activity. Since HSSs are associated to coronal structures visible in extreme-ultraviolet observations, this provides a natural basis for forecasting several days in advance. In this work, we investigate whether the topology of coronal structures observed in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) images contains predictive information on the subsequent occurrence of CH-driven HSSs at Earth. To this end, we consider Topological Data Analysis (TDA), and in particular persistent homology, to classify EUV solar images according to the occurrence of HSSs at Earth four days later. The target is a binary classification of HSS occurrence at a four-day lead time, defined using an HSS interval catalog and solar wind speed thresholds. Several combinations of topological representations and classifiers are evaluated under a common cross-validation framework. The results indicate that the topology of EUV coronal structures alone contains predictive information on subsequent CH-driven HSS occurrence, despite the absence of explicit CH geometric descriptors in the model input. To investigate the origin of this predictive information, we develop a model-level explainability framework based on cross-validation-aggregated feature weights and spatial evidence maps. A fully traced example connects persistence diagrams and persistence-image features to the classifier output and to their spatial localization in the original EUV observation. The proposed framework provides a transparent and computationally lightweight approach for investigating the relationship between coronal topology and subsequent high-speed solar wind streams.

candidate.title: Towards a Unified Framework of Optimal Input-Side Dimensional Configuration for Deep CTR Prediction
candidate.abstract: Deep click-through rate (CTR) prediction has achieved substantial success through increasingly expressive feature interaction architectures. However, predictive performance also depends on how input-side information is configured before interaction modeling. Existing studies have shown that selecting informative samples, features, or embedding units can improve prediction accuracy. Nevertheless, they primarily optimize these selection mechanisms independently along a single input-side dimension, overlooking their shared basic form and the inherent dependencies across input levels, thereby limiting the effectiveness of input-side dimensional configuration. To address this issue, we propose OptIDC, a unified framework for Optimal Input-side Dimensional Configuration in deep CTR prediction. OptIDC jointly learns sample, feature, and embedding-unit level configurations within a unified framework by integrating their corresponding selection mechanisms. To explicitly coordinate selection decisions across different levels, OptIDC further introduces a selection-weighted Optimal Transport mechanism that aligns coarse- and fine-grained selections via transport over finite measures, thereby alleviating cross-level selection conflicts while preserving the semantics of each input level. Moreover, OptIDC is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing CTR models. Extensive experiments on four real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that OptIDC consistently achieves higher AUC than existing input-side selection methods, validating the effectiveness of unified input-side dimensional configuration.

candidate.title: Implementasi Pendekatan Komunikatif pada Mata Kuliah Muhadatsah Mahasiswa Prodi Pendidikan Bahasa Arab STAI Al-Gazali Soppeng
candidate.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan implementasi pendekatan komunikatif dalam pembelajaran Muhadatsah serta dampaknya terhadap kemampuan berbicara mahasiswa Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Arab STAI Al-Gazali Soppeng. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan subjek mahasiswa yang mengikuti mata kuliah Muhadatsah. Teknik pengumpulan data meliputi observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, sedangkan analisis data dilakukan melalui tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan komunikatif diimplementasikan melalui berbagai aktivitas berbasis komunikasi, seperti dialog, diskusi kelompok, bermain peran, dan simulasi percakapan kontekstual. Pendekatan ini mampu menciptakan suasana pembelajaran yang komunikatif dan partisipatif, meningkatkan keberanian, kelancaran, serta kepercayaan diri mahasiswa dalam berbicara bahasa Arab. Selain itu, pendekatan komunikatif juga berdampak positif terhadap motivasi dan keaktifan mahasiswa serta mendorong perubahan peran dosen sebagai fasilitator pembelajaran. Dengan demikian, pendekatan komunikatif dinilai efektif dalam meningkatkan kualitas pembelajaran Muhadatsah dan kompetensi komunikatif mahasiswa dalam keterampilan berbicara bahasa Arab.

candidate.title: ФОРМУВАННЯ ПРИРОДНИЧИХ УЯВЛЕНЬ І ПОНЯТЬ У ДІТЕЙ ДОШКІЛЬНОГО ВІКУ ІЗ ЗАСТОСУВАННЯМ АЛЬТЕРНАТИВНОЇ ТА ДОДАТКОВОЇ КОМУНІКАЦІЇ В ОСВІТНЬОМУ НАПРЯМІ «ДИТИНА В ПРИРОДНОМУ ДОВКІЛЛІ»
candidate.abstract: У статті розкрито особливості формування природничих уявлень і понять у дітей дошкільного віку з особливими освітніми потребами засобами альтернативної та додаткової комунікації. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена необхідністю забезпечення доступності освітнього процесу для дітей із порушеннями мовлення, розладами аутистичного спектра, інтелектуальними та комплексними порушеннями розвитку в умовах інклюзивної дошкільної освіти. Метою статті є теоретичне обґрунтування педагогічного потенціалу альтернативної та додаткової комунікації у процесі формування природничих уявлень і понять у дітей дошкільного віку в освітньому напрямі «Дитина в природному довкіллі». У дослідженні використано комплекс теоретичних методів: аналіз психолого-педагогічної, методичної та спеціальної літератури; узагальнення сучасних наукових підходів до організації інклюзивного освітнього середовища; систематизацію засобів альтернативної та додаткової комунікації та визначення їх педагогічних можливостей у природничо-пізнавальній діяльності дітей. Проаналізовано особливості використання низькотехнологічних і високотехнологічних засобів комунікації, зокрема жестів, піктограм, карток Picture Exchange Communication System, комунікативних таблиць, візуальних розкладів, електронних комунікаторів і мобільних застосунків. Результати дослідження свідчать, що використання альтернативної та додаткової комунікації забезпечує візуальну підтримку освітнього процесу, сприяє розвитку мовлення, сенсорного сприймання, пізнавальної активності та формуванню елементарних природничих узагальнень. Встановлено, що поєднання спостережень, практичної діяльності, елементарних дослідів і дидактичних ігор із засобами візуальної підтримки підвищує доступність навчального матеріалу та активізує участь дітей у пізнавальній діяльності. Визначено педагогічні умови ефективного використання альтернативної та додаткової комунікації: індивідуальний добір засобів комунікації, систематичність їх використання, поєднання мовленнєвої, візуальної та практичної підтримки, а також взаємодія педагогів і батьків. Зроблено висновок, що альтернативна та додаткова комунікація є ефективним засобом формування природничих уявлень і понять у дітей дошкільного віку з особливими освітніми потребами, оскільки забезпечує доступність освітнього процесу, підтримує комунікативну діяльність та створює умови для активного пізнання навколишнього світу.

candidate.title: Influence of Online Learning Quality, Lecturer Support, and Academic Self-Efficacy on Student Engagement
candidate.abstract: The rapid expansion of online learning in higher education has transformed the way students interact with course content, instructors, and peers, making student engagement a critical indicator of learning success. This study investigates the influence of online learning quality, lecturer support, and academic self-efficacy on student engagement in an online learning environment. Using a quantitative research design, data were collected from university students through a structured questionnaire measuring the four key constructs. The data were analyzed using multiple regression analysis to examine the direct effects of each independent variable on student engagement. The results reveal that all three variables—online learning quality, lecturer support, and academic self-efficacy—have significant positive effects on student engagement. Among these, academic self-efficacy emerged as the strongest predictor, indicating that students’ confidence in their academic abilities plays a central role in shaping their level of participation and involvement. Online learning quality also significantly contributes to engagement, emphasizing the importance of well-designed, interactive, and accessible digital learning environments. Additionally, lecturer support was found to positively influence engagement, highlighting the role of instructor presence, feedback, and communication in fostering an engaging learning experience. These findings suggest that improving both structural and psychological aspects of online education can enhance student engagement. The study contributes to the growing body of literature on online learning by providing empirical evidence on key factors that influence engagement and offers practical implications for educators and institutions aiming to optimize online learning experiences.

candidate.title: Meta-Sintesis Pancasila Sebagai Ideologi atau Pemikiran Filosofis: Sebuah Tinjauan Kritis dalam Perspektif Komunikasi
candidate.abstract: Pancasila is often debated as either an ideology or a philosophical system of thought, while a gap between its values and everyday practice persists. This study aims to quantitatively synthesize the strength of the relationship between understanding and practicing Pancasila values and citizen behavior, such as tolerance and radical attitudes. It uses Koento Wibisono's dimensions of ideology (belief, myth, loyalty) and the three philosophical principles (ontology, epistemology, axiology) as its framework, with the way values are delivered treated as a moderator. The study was designed as a meta-analysis using a random-effects model and Fisher's z transformation. A search of the Garuda and Google Scholar databases for publications from 1996 to 2026 yielded twenty articles as an initial corpus. All were conceptual, normative, or qualitative, so effect sizes could not yet be pooled and the three hypotheses could not be tested statistically. A thematic synthesis shows that ideology and philosophy are understood as a unity, that Pancasila values are hierarchical, and that their practice remains suboptimal, while rote-based education leaves little lasting impression. The corpus only hints at a positive relationship between internalizing Pancasila and tolerance. This study contributes a coding scheme for future research and recommends strengthening programs that emphasize role modeling, character education, and value delivery suited to technological developments.

candidate.title: PENINGKATAN MINAT BELAJAR IPA MELALUI PENERAPAN PEMBELAJARAN MENDALAM DENGAN PRINSIP TEACHING AT THE RIGHT LEVEL PADA MURID KELAS VIII
candidate.abstract: Penelitian tindakan kelas ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan perubahan minat belajar IPA murid kelas VIII melalui penerapan model Discovery Learning dengan pendekatan Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL). Penelitian dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, yaitu materi tekanan hidrostatis melalui percobaan botol berlubang pada Siklus I dan Hukum Archimedes melalui percobaan benda dalam air pada Siklus II. Subjek analisis terdiri atas 25 murid yang memiliki data lengkap untuk dibandingkan pada tahap pra-siklus, Siklus I, dan Siklus II. Data minat belajar dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner berisi 12 pernyataan yang mencakup empat indikator, yaitu keterlibatan aktif, perhatian dan fokus, perasaan senang atau kenyamanan, serta ketekunan dan kemauan berusaha. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif melalui perhitungan rata-rata skor dan indeks persentase. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata indeks minat belajar meningkat dari 95,89% pada pra-siklus menjadi 96,33% pada Siklus I, kemudian mencapai 99,33% pada Siklus II. Peningkatan dari pra-siklus hingga Siklus II sebesar 3,44 poin persentase. Pada Siklus II, seluruh indikator mengalami peningkatan dibandingkan Siklus I, dengan keterlibatan aktif mencapai indeks 100%. Hasil ini menunjukkan kecenderungan peningkatan indeks minat belajar selama pelaksanaan tindakan. Namun, indeks awal yang tinggi dan penggunaan kuesioner sebagai instrumen utama perlu dipertimbangkan dalam menafsirkan hasil. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa penerapan Discovery Learning dengan pendekatan TaRL diikuti peningkatan deskriptif indeks minat belajar murid dalam pembelajaran IPA.

candidate.title: أثر استخدام خرائط التفكير في تدريس النحو على مهارة تركيب الجمل العربية لدى طلاب بمعهد الإمام الشاطبي
candidate.abstract: This study aims to find out the effect of using mind maps in teaching grammar on sentence construction skills among tenth-grade students at Imam Al-Shatibi Institute for Quran Memorization in the Islamic Unit, South Sulawesi. The problem is that some students struggle to understand grammar rules and apply them correctly when forming Arabic sentences. The researcher used a quantitative method with a quasi-experimental design. The study sample consisted of an experimental group of 27 students and a control group of 24 students. Data were collected using pre-tests and post-tests and analyzed using IBM SPSS through normality and homogeneity tests and the independent-samples t-test. The results showed that the average score of the experimental group rose from 66.51 in the pre-test to 79.29 in the post-test, while the average score of the control group was 72.62 in the post-test. The statistical significance (Sig. 2-tailed) was 0.001, which is less than the 0.05 significance level, indicating a statistically significant effect of using mind maps in teaching grammar to improve students' Arabic sentence construction skills.

candidate.title: Problematika Pembelajaran PAI dalam Membentuk Akhlak Peserta Didik di Era Digital
candidate.abstract: This article aims to analyze the problems faced by Islamic Religious Education (PAI) in shaping students’ morals amid the development of social media. This research employs a qualitative method with a library research approach by examining scholarly journals on digital morality, Islamic education, social media etiquette, teacher role modelling, and digital literacy. The literature synthesis indicates that social media has become an environment that can influence students’ values and behavior. The issues discussed include exposure to content that contradicts Islamic values, impolite communication, cyberbullying, dependence on peer approval, and the gap between students’ understanding of Islamic values and their application in digital behavior. Nevertheless, social media also has the potential to serve as a medium for moral education when used appropriately. This study emphasizes the importance of teacher role modelling, digital literacy, habituation of Islamic values, contextual learning, and collaboration among schools, families, and communities. The fundamental issue to consider is how to connect students’ religious understanding acquired through classroom learning with the application of moral values in everyday life, including their use of social media. Therefore, PAI learning should focus not only on religious knowledge but also on developing students’ ability to apply Islamic ethics critically, wisely, and consistently in digital spaces.

candidate.title: FILOLOGIK TAJRIBA-SINOV ISHLARINI TASHKIL ETISH MAZMUNI, BOSQICHLARI VA DIAGNOSTIK MEZONLARI
candidate.abstract: Mazkur maqolada filologik yo‘nalishdagi tajriba-sinov ishlarini tashkil etishning ilmiy-metodik asoslari, mazmuni, asosiy bosqichlari hamda diagnostik mezonlari yoritilgan. Filologik ta’lim jarayonida tajriba-sinov ishlarini tashkil etishda tadqiqot maqsadi, vazifalari, obyekti va predmetini aniqlash, tajriba va nazorat guruhlarini shakllantirish, diagnostik vositalarni tanlash, olingan natijalarni miqdoriy va sifat jihatdan tahlil qilishning ahamiyati ochib berilgan. Shuningdek, talabalarning lingvistik bilimlari, matnni tahlil qilish ko‘nikmalari, nutqiy kompetensiyasi, mustaqil fikrlashi, ijodiy yondashuvi va refleksiv faoliyatini baholash imkonini beruvchi diagnostik mezonlar tavsiflangan. Tajriba-sinov ishlarining aniqlovchi, shakllantiruvchi va nazorat bosqichlari o‘zaro uzviy jarayon sifatida tahlil qilinib, ularni ilmiy asosda tashkil etish filologik ta’lim samaradorligini oshirishning muhim sharti ekanligi asoslangan.

candidate.title: The motivational impact of numeracy-based think pair share in elementary science education
candidate.abstract: Purpose: to examine the effectiveness of numeracy-based think-pair-share (TPS) in improving grade V students’ learning motivation in IPAS compared with conventional instruction. Method: this study used a quasi-experimental design with 20 grade V students in experimental and control groups. Data were collected through pretest and posttest motivation questionnaires and analyzed using N-Gain. Findings: showed that numeracy-based TPS improved students’ learning motivation, with a mean increase of 21.39 points and an N-Gain of 0.68, compared with 10.12 points and an N-Gain of 0.32 in the control group. These findings suggest that numeracy-based TPS is a promising approach to enhancing motivation in elementary IPAS learning. Implications: this study highlights the potential of numeracy-based TPS as an innovative instructional strategy to enhance student motivation through active participation, peer collaboration, and meaningful numeracy activities in elementary IPAS learning. Originality: lies in integrating numeracy literacy with the think-pair-share (TPS) model to enhance students’ learning motivation in elementary IPAS, an approach that remains limited in previous research.

candidate.title: Metacognition and Attitude as Predictors of Conceptual Understanding in Physics: A Complementary Approach
candidate.abstract: Background: Complementary approach provides an opportunity for students to connect pre-class, in-class, and post-class activities. Objectives: This study examined the correlations and predictive effects of metacognition and attitude on learners' conceptual understanding in physics using a complementary approach. Method: A quasi-experimental, pretest-posttest, non-equivalent control group design was used. A sample of 173 natural science students from two Ethiopian secondary schools was randomly assigned to experimental (CAIM instruction) and control (traditional teaching) groups. Data were collected using FCCUT, MCQ, and LAS instruments and analyzed via Pearson correlations and hierarchical multiple regression at p = 0.05. Results: The two variables showed positive and statistically significant correlations with students' conceptual understanding of physics: metacognition (r = 0.30) and attitude (r = 0.31), p < 0.01. Further, both metacognition (R² = 0.15, f² = 0.08) and attitude (R² = 0.16, f² = 0.10), ΔR² = 0.08, p < 0.001, predicted 8% of the varience in conceptual understanding when CAIM was employed. Conclusion: We recommend that physics teachers could apply the CAIM when teaching physics, as it allows students to develop a positive correlation between the predictor variables and conceptual understanding, though their correlations are moderate.

candidate.title: Professional Maritime Character: What Really Matters?
candidate.abstract: This study examines the factors associated with Professional Maritime Character among vocational maritime students by investigating the effects of Islamic Work Ethic, Religious Commitment, and Spiritual Intelligence, while considering Self-Discipline as a mediating mechanism and Moral Awareness as a moderating factor. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed involving 525 students from Batch VIII, X, and XI at Politeknik Pelayaran Sumatera Barat, Indonesia, using a total sampling technique. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling with the PLS Algorithm and Bootstrapping Calculation. The measurement model demonstrated adequate indicator reliability, internal consistency, and convergent validity across all constructs. The structural results show that Islamic Work Ethic, Religious Commitment, and Spiritual Intelligence have significant positive effects on Professional Maritime Character, while Religious Commitment significantly predicts Self-Discipline; however, Islamic Work Ethic and Spiritual Intelligence do not significantly predict Self-Discipline. Moral Awareness has a significant negative direct association with Professional Maritime Character, but its interactions with Islamic Work Ethic, Religious Commitment, and Spiritual Intelligence are not significant. These findings indicate that professional maritime character is more strongly associated with the direct internalization of religious and spiritual values than with conditional effects of moral awareness, providing practical implications for integrated character development in maritime vocational education.

candidate.title: Pengaruh Pengalaman Praktik Kerja Industri Dan Motivasi Belajar Terhadap Hasil Belajar Rencana Anggaran Biaya Siswa DPIB SMK Negeri 1 Baureno.
candidate.abstract: Cost estimation (Rencana Anggaran Biaya, RAB) is a course that demands careful calculation and an understanding of how costs arise in real projects. An initial observation at SMK Negeri 1 Baureno found that roughly 63% of students grasped and could apply RAB concepts. This research examines whether industrial internship (Prakerin) experience and learning motivation, individually and jointly, influence the RAB learning outcomes of Building Modeling and Information Design (DPIB) students. It adopts an associative quantitative approach with an ex post facto design. Purposive sampling selected 68 twelfth-grade students who had finished their internship. Four-point Likert questionnaires measured Prakerin experience and learning motivation, while a multiple-choice test and grade records supplied the outcome data. Classical assumption tests and multiple linear regression were run in SPSS. Prakerin experience had a significant positive effect on outcomes (B = 1.137, t = 2.717, p = 0.008); the effect of motivation was positive but not significant (B = 0.782, t = 1.754, p = 0.084). Together, the two variables had a significant effect (F = 44.231, p < 0.001), explaining 57.6% of the variance. Schools should improve internship quality and link students' industry experience to RAB teaching

candidate.title: MAKTABGACHA YOSHDAGI BOLALARDA KOMMUNIKATIV KOMPETENSIYANI RIVOJLANTIRISHNING PEDAGOGIK SHART-SHAROITLARI
candidate.abstract: Mazkur maqolada maktabgacha yoshdagi bolalarda kommunikativ kompetensiyani rivojlantirishning pedagogik shart-sharoitlari, nutqiy faollikni oshirishga xizmat qiluvchi ta’limiy yondashuvlar hamda pedagog va ota-onalarning o‘zaro hamkorligi masalalari yoritilgan. Shuningdek, bolalarda o‘z fikrini erkin ifodalash, suhbatdoshni tinglash, savol-javob jarayonida faol ishtirok etish va tengdoshlari bilan samarali muloqot o‘rnatish ko‘nikmalarini shakllantirishning pedagogik imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. Maktabgacha ta’lim jarayonida o‘yin, muammoli vaziyatlar, rolli mashg‘ulotlar va dialogik nutqni rivojlantirishga qaratilgan faoliyatlardan foydalanishning ahamiyati asoslab berilgan.

candidate.title: Afetos e fórmulas: Autoetnografia da relação professor-aluno e o desenvolvimento cognitivo na matemática
candidate.abstract: A aprendizagem da Matemática é historicamente marcada por bloqueios emocionais, ansiedade e elevados índices de rejeição entre os estudantes, desafios que frequentemente ultrapassam a dimensão puramente cognitiva. Diante disso, este artigo analisa a importância da relação professor-aluno no processo de ensino e aprendizagem da Matemática, destacando como os aspectos afetivos e o diálogo horizontal podem potencializar o desenvolvimento cognitivo. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como um ensaio teórico-reflexivo de abordagem qualitativa, pautado na revisão bibliográfica e na pesquisa narrativa, articulando os aportes teóricos de Wallon, Vygotsky, Freire, D'Ambrosio e Charlot às vivências da práxis docente do autor ao longo de 16 anos de magistério. A análise de episódios práticos — como a ressignificação da atitude de um aluno com aversão à disciplina, a aplicação de uma gincana colaborativa e o trabalho com o ensino de jovens e adultos (EJA) — evidencia que o acolhimento, o respeito e a valorização das trajetórias individuais constituem uma engrenagem essencial para a superação de traumas e o despertar da autonomia intelectual. Os resultados indicam que a afetividade não se contrapõe ao rigor científico, mas atua como elemento estruturante que transforma a sala de aula em um ambiente seguro de cooperação e de aprendizagem significativa. Conclui-se que integrar a afetividade e a cognição é indispensável para humanizar o ensino da Matemática e promover uma formação democrática e emancipatória.

candidate.title: Hubungan Kepemimpinan Partisipatif dengan Etos Kerja Tenaga Kependidikan pada Perguruan Tinggi Vokasi
candidate.abstract: This quantitative correlational study examined the relationship between participative leadership and work ethic among 30 educational support staff at a higher education institution in Medan, Indonesia. The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design to determine the strength and direction of the relationship between the two variables. Total sampling was applied, involving all 30 staff members as research respondents. Data were collected using a questionnaire comprising eight five-point Likert-scale items for each variable. Instrument reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha, yielding coefficients of 0.781 for participative leadership and 0.792 for work ethic, indicating acceptable internal consistency. Normality was examined using the Shapiro–Wilk test, which indicated that the participative leadership total score deviated from a normal distribution. Consequently, Spearman’s rank correlation was selected as the primary statistical analysis. The results revealed a positive and statistically significant association between participative leadership and work ethic (ρ = 0.758, p < .001). These findings suggest that higher participative leadership scores tend to accompany higher work ethic scores. However, the results establish an association rather than a causal relationship and should be interpreted cautiously because the study involved one institution and relied on self-reported questionnaire data.

candidate.title: Pengaruh AI Readiness, AI Job Crafting, dan Perceived Career Uncertainty Terhadap Career Adaptability pada Mahasiswa Yang Bekerja
candidate.abstract: Kemajuan kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence/AI) mengubah kemampuan yang dicari di tempat kerja, sehingga adaptabilitas karier menjadi bekal penting bagi mahasiswa yang kuliah sambil bekerja. Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh kesiapan AI (AI readiness), pembentukan pekerjaan berbasis AI (AI job crafting), dan ketidakpastian karier yang dirasakan (perceived career uncertainty) terhadap adaptabilitas karier (career adaptability) pada mahasiswa yang bekerja. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner daring 24 butir dari 109 mahasiswa yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling, lalu dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda atas skor rata-rata tiap variabel. PLS-SEM yang semula direncanakan tidak dipakai karena model pengukurannya tidak memenuhi kriteria (AVE < 0,50). Hasilnya, AI readiness (β = 0,428; p < 0,001) dan AI job crafting (β = 0,248; p = 0,002) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan. Perceived career uncertainty berpengaruh signifikan tetapi positif (β = 0,216; p = 0,005), sehingga H3 yang menduga arah negatif tidak didukung. Ketiga variabel bersama-sama menjelaskan 51,8% varians career adaptability (R² = 0,518; F = 37,64; p < 0,001). Meski demikian, reliabilitas instrumen rendah (Cronbach's alpha −2,08 sampai 0,47) dan data memuat banyak pola jawaban yang berulang, sehingga temuan perlu dibaca dengan hati-hati.
